A public research university (38,000 students) — Education & Research engagement delivered by a 14-person team over 12 months, US scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: At-risk students surfaced at failure; LMS/SIS/support data siloed.
GenAI governance vacuum; integrity disputes rising.

blocks.x: The student-success platform unified SIS/LMS/support data with outcome lineage; early-warning models feed advising orchestration (Swarm) with case management; and the integrity infrastructure deployed policy rails plus logged assistive AI per course under faculty-governance sign-off.

What the delivery actually looks like week to week: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per cohort performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. from week 3 the working slice goes live at region scope: shadow first, then canary, then promoted cohorts — each promotion justified by the eval gate, not enthusiasm. industrialization (weeks 9–12) is where most vendors stop; we treat it as the deliverable: your team runs it, our evidence pack survives your auditor, and the delta is signed. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision — that is the point of signing baselines.

items: Reported as down 62 against baseline, reproducible by your analysts from the method note
The committed move on this metric: down 14, measured against the baseline signed in week two
